column3: Close to the Greek.
“Loathsome, malignant sores broke out” renders “there came a harmful and grievous sore.”
“Turned to” renders “became”; “living thing” renders “soul of life.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “O Holy One” and no “O Lord”; the Textus Receptus has “O Lord … and holy.” “Brought these judgments” renders “judged these things.”
“As they deserve” renders “they are worthy.”
BSB follows the critical text with “the altar” (the Textus Receptus has “another from the altar”). “Reply” renders λέγοντος (“saying”).
“Power” is added.
“Cursed” renders ἐβλασφήμησαν (“blasphemed”).
“Was plunged into darkness” renders “became darkened”; “men began to” is added.
“Curse” renders ἐβλασφήμησαν (“blasphemed”).
“The kings of the East” renders “the kings from the rising of the sun.”
“That looked like frogs” renders “as frogs.”
BSB follows the critical text with “the great day” (no “that”). “Demonic spirits” renders “spirits of demons”; “all the kings of the earth” renders “the kings of the whole inhabited world.”
BSB puts the verse in quotation marks; “remains awake and clothed” recasts “watching and keeping his garments.”
“The kings” is added; “they assembled” renders the singular συνήγαγεν.
BSB follows the critical text, “from the throne in the temple,” with no “of heaven.”
BSB follows the critical-text order (“lightning, rumblings, thunder”).
“God remembered Babylon … and gave her” recasts “Babylon was remembered before God, to give her.”
Close to the Greek.
“Weighing almost a hundred pounds” renders ταλαντιαία (“a talent in weight”); “on them from above” renders “out of heaven upon men.”
